Which one of these propositions does this manifesto's first principle mainly express? Choose none if it expresses none of them.

Options:
- competence: People must build their own competence before relying on AI, and whether they can still do the work without the tool must be tested.
- situation: Change situations, defaults and incentives rather than relying on warnings, labels or individual vigilance.
- monoculture: A central new risk is monoculture: a few models or one smooth answer become the default route to knowledge, so answers should show where experts disagree rather than a single consensus.
- independent_sources: Corroboration must count independent sources, not repetitions of the same source (including many AI outputs drawing on the same data).
- cite_by_default: AI answers should cite or link to their sources by default and send readers to them.
- external_audits: AI systems must be audited on their behavior by parties independent of the vendor.
- accountable_owner: Every deployed AI system has a named accountable owner who bears liability for it.
- stop_counting_papers: Stop using publication counts, rankings and journal metrics to evaluate researchers and institutions.
- pay_coarsely: Money for the knowledge commons should flow coarsely to communities and institutions (pools, funds, dues), not as per-item or per-retrieval payments.
- telemetry: AI systems must log what they retrieved and used, and independent parties must have the right to audit those logs.
- antitrust_safe_harbour: Knowledge producers should be able to bargain collectively with AI firms as a bloc, including through an antitrust safe harbour.
- levy: A levy, tax or mandatory dues on AI firms should fund the knowledge commons, at least as a backstop if voluntary deals fail.
- training_vs_grounding: Permissions for using content to train models should be separate from permissions for retrieving it to ground answers.
- consent_to_train: Being openly readable does not make a work open to AI training: training use requires the rights holders' or creators' consent (opt-in), at least for some classes of work.
- honour_licences: AI reusers must honor the licenses chosen by open knowledge projects such as Wikipedia, and heavy reusers should fund the infrastructure they draw on.
- refusal_fundable: A community's refusal to have its knowledge taken or used is legitimate, binding and should be funded, not penalized.
- forkable_infrastructure: Knowledge infrastructure must be forkable and allow exit: open data and open source, with copies outside any one jurisdiction or company.
- profiting_counter: Whoever profits from a count or metric must not set or control it.
- southern_governance: Global South institutions, diamond open-access journals and similar communities must hold binding governance power, with funded seats, in the bodies and funds being created.
- identify_agents_not_readers: Automated agents and coordinated campaigns should be identified, but human readers should not be; anonymity is preserved.
- failure_data: Failures, errors, null and negative results are first-class data that must be published and preserved.
- charter_for_every_body: The bodies that check (auditors, fact-checkers, the new funds and institutions) must be paid and bound in advance by a public charter that answers who guards the guards.
- hitl_not_safeguard: A human in the loop is not by itself a safeguard: people over-rely on AI and adopt its errors and biases.
- seat_floor_novelty: Any gatekeeper, human or machine (such as an AI reviewer), must pass a published performance test before it is trusted, including the ability to recognize novelty.
- no_ai_intimate_roles: AI should not stand in for people in intimate roles such as companionship for children, grief or therapy.
- global_majority_hopeful: People in the global majority / Global South are more hopeful about AI than this room, and that hope should shape the agenda.
- environmental_costs: The environmental costs of AI and the human costs of moderation and data work belong in the ledger.
- apprenticeship: Apprenticeships, entry-level jobs and the training of new experts and checkers must be funded, because AI erodes the path from novice to expert.
- absent_voices: The document names who was missing from the room and commits to including them in a future convening.
- b_accelerant: Most of the crisis predates AI: AI accelerates old failures, so remedies must distinguish what was already broken from what AI newly breaks.
- b_describe_precisely: AI systems should be described by what they actually do, neither as minds or oracles nor as mere autocomplete.
- b_evaluation_scarce: Evaluation and verification, not production, are now the scarce resource, so investment should shift from producing knowledge to checking it.
- b_credibility_process: Credibility should rest on checkable process, track record and accountable people or communities, not on fluency, polish or credentials.
- b_provenance_infrastructure: Provenance and attribution are infrastructure that must be built into knowledge systems and AI tools.
- b_pay_human_labor: The human labor behind trustworthy knowledge (reviewing, editing, curating, checking) must be made visible and paid.
- b_strengthen_judgment: AI tools should be designed to strengthen human judgment and capability rather than replace it.
- b_no_single_owner: No single company, state or model should control the infrastructure of knowledge; concentrated control of it is a central risk that needs public options or governance.
- b_public_investment: Knowledge institutions and the knowledge commons are public goods that deserve public investment and independence from platforms and states.
- none: none of the above

Title: Writing Is Now Cheaper Than Reading: A Manifesto for Sustaining Human Knowledge
First principle: AI is widening pre-existing cracks in the knowledge system, so each problem needs its own diagnosis, avoiding both blanket 'AI crisis' blame and complacency, and testing harm claims rigorously.
